In March 1830, George Turnbull joined Telford at Abingdon Street as a clerk and draughtsman
Telford's appointment as Engineer was initially shared with William Jessop the senior consulting engineer
From his initial appointment in July 1815, he was paid 5 guineas a day plus 2s a mile.
His presence in Shropshire enabled his appointment as "General agent (…) engineer (…) overlooker of the Works" on the Ellesmere canal
Later holdings were for the Macclesfield Canal on which Telford was consulted, and more substantially on the St Katharine Docks.
Telford's appointment as Engineer was initially shared with William Jessop the senior consulting engineer
From 1800 he had a presence in London, for many years at the Salopian Coffee House, Charing Cross

His presence in Shropshire enabled his appointment as "General agent (…) engineer (…) overlooker of the Works" on the Ellesmere canal at a salary of £500 p.a. in September 1793, William Jessop being consultant.
